about.title: Personal Injury Help in Soledad, California
about.longDescription: Soledad may be a smaller community, but collisions still happen here, and they can upend a family's routine overnight. Public records for the most recent year show 12 injury collisions and 19 people hurt on city streets, with reports clustering along Front Street, Monterey Street, Metz Road, and Gabilan Drive. Saturday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. tend to see more reported crashes than other times, likely tied to weekend traffic patterns through town. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in a fall, workplace accident, or other injury event anywhere in Soledad, sorting out next steps while you're also trying to heal can feel overwhelming. We listen to what happened and help you understand your options. There's no cost to talk with us, and we only get paid if we recover money for you. You don't have to figure out California's legal system alone, and you don't have to decide anything on this first call.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us Before the Clock Runs Out

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, and claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can end your right to recover, so it helps to understand your timeline early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Stop You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for what happened. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Ordinary California injury cases have no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. We can help you understand what that could mean for your specific case.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee. We only get paid out of a settlement or award, which means our incentive lines up with getting you the best possible result.

items.answer: Nothing. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in Soledad?
items.answer: In most California injury cases you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a public road or vehicle, that window can shrink to as little as six months for a claim notice, so it's worth checking your timeline sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover damages even if you were partially at fault. Your compensation would be reduced by your share of responsibility, but it isn't automatically barred.

items.question: Are certain roads in Soledad more prone to reported crashes?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Front Street, Monterey Street, Metz Road, and Gabilan Drive have some of the higher reported collision counts in the city, and Saturday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. show more activity than other times. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.
